note: Owed work done: 24 Genius lyric pages fetched live (22 in-folder canon tracks + 2 ask-named tracks verified absent from the folder), grammar extracted and compression study written to watch/inbox/music/lyric-archaeology.md; gaps honestly named: the operator's 14-line riddle text was NOT found on disk (searched watch/inbox, memory, state, queue, all gala folders; only false-positive hits), so the study measures against the ask's own riddle spec (14 lines, clock, stakes, reversal, exit line); Phoenix is not in the folder's 51-artist taxonomy and 'dance with trouble' is unresolvable to any track; no code under mag/ or tools/ was touched so the violation ratchet was not run (not required by the ask in that case).
decision_changed: lyric-workover rewrite form: the 14-line riddle rewrite must obey the canon's measured grammar (I/you present tense, 4-8 word single-clause lines, hook as instruction or count at 1-4 words per line, reversal delivered as ONE mutated word inside an otherwise identical repeated line, exit line 1-4 words and loop-ready, clock and stakes staged as objects never stated, one beat per 3.5-4 lines, no thesis anywhere) instead of prose-thriller conventions

rows.claim: The canon's hooks repeat 30-144x and sing about repetition itself, so the rewrite must mark which of its 14 lines are the loop rather than writing 14 through-composed lines.
rows.quote: Over And Over's thesis line is "The joy of repetition really is in you" and the song loops; One More Time's title phrase appears 30+ times as the celebration itself; Around the World is one phrase 144 times.
rows.steal: Composer lane: before drafting, mark the loop lines (2, 6 and 10 identical except one word) in the rewrite's line plan; land the plan as a comment atop the rewrite file.
rows.falsifier: A canonical in-folder track whose hook is stated once and never repeated (a through-composed hook) kills this law; all 24 fetched tracks loop.

rows.claim: The canon never announces a turn: its reversals are a single swapped word inside an otherwise identical repeated line (feel/look in Over And Over, would/wouldn't in Heartbeats).
rows.quote: Over And Over's chorus repeats verbatim except its last line, swapping "when I feel this way" for "when you look this way": the whole perspective flips in one word.
rows.steal: Build the rewrite's reversal as exactly one mutated word in the repeated line, landed at the line-10 position of the 14.
rows.falsifier: A canon track whose reversal arrives as a new sentence or new scene rather than a word-swap inside an identical line.

rows.claim: Stakes are never named as emotions: grief is a phone call and coffee, doom is a car and a bottle, obsession is a burning home; each beat gets one object staged flat.
rows.steal: Cast the riddle's clock and stakes as one object each (a phone, a key, a car) in beats 1-2 of the rewrite; land in its first 4-line block.
rows.falsifier: A fetched canon track that names an abstract emotion (grief, fear, dread) directly as its stake.

rows.claim: The canon measures time by counting, never by explaining: one-two-three-four, ten days, hour after hour, one more time.
rows.quote: The canon counts instead of explaining duration; a number plus a repeated line IS a clock.
rows.steal: Open the rewrite with a count line (one, two, three, four mode) as the clock; land as line 1.
rows.falsifier: A canon track that carries its timespan in explanatory prose with no number or count anywhere.

rows.claim: Exit lines are 1-4 words and are placed where the loop restarts, so the ending is a beginning (go slow; work is never over; Downtown).
rows.quote: Exit lines are 1 to 4 words, placed where the loop restarts, so the song ends by becoming the beginning.
rows.steal: End the rewrite on a 1-4 word loop-ready line; land as lines 13-14.
rows.falsifier: A canon track that ends on a long (8+ word) resolved moral or summary line.

rows.claim: Across 24 fetched lyric sheets, zero tracks state a thesis in the hook, resolve the plot, or name abstract emotions; the form shows a feeling and makes you do it.
rows.quote: The canon shows a feeling and makes you do it; it never tells you what to think about it.
rows.steal: Gate the rewrite pre-submit: no line may state the story's meaning or resolve it; land the gate as a check in the composer lane's ask.
rows.falsifier: A fetched canon track whose hook states its own thesis as an argument.

rows.claim: The canon holds one story beat per 3.5-4 unique lines (Heartbeats: 4 beats in ~16 unique lines; Someone Great: the call beat in 8), so the riddle's 4 beats in 14 lines is inside the band and the form can hold the thriller minus its connective tissue.
rows.quote: Verdict: the riddle's 4 beats in 14 lines sits exactly inside the canon's measured band of one beat per 3.5 to 4 lines.
rows.steal: Budget the rewrite 14 lines as three 4-line beat blocks plus a 2-line exit; land the budget as the rewrite's line plan.
rows.falsifier: A canon verse cleanly holding 4 beats in under 10 lines, or needing 20+ lines for 4 beats, would break the 3.5-4 band.
